title: Momentum Module 5 Lesson 1: Kinetic Energy Loss In Collisions custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ moving with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ on a smooth horizontal surface. Immediately after the collision, $A$ moves with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $B$ moves with speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the system caused by the collision.

Particle $P$ of mass $1.0\text{ kg}$ moving with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal track collides with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $2.0\text{ kg}$ and coalesces with it. Calculate the percentage of the initial kinetic energy that is lost during the collision.

Particles $A$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ and $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ move towards each other on a smooth horizontal plane with speeds $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. The particles collide and coalesce. Calculate the loss of kinetic energy caused by the collision.

A particle of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ travels horizontally with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a smooth vertical barrier. The particle hits the barrier and rebounds. Given that $6.4\text{ J}$ of kinetic energy is lost during the impact, calculate the speed with which the particle rebounds.

Particle $A$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ moving with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ on a smooth horizontal table. Immediately after the collision, $A$ is brought to rest and $B$ moves with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Show that no kinetic energy is lost in this collision.

Particle $M$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ travels with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal surface and collides with a stationary particle $N$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. The two particles coalesce upon impact. Calculate the fraction of the initial kinetic energy that is retained by the system.

questions.prompt: Two small spheres $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.8\text{ kg}$ and $0.4\text{ kg}$ respectively, move towards each other on a smooth horizontal table with speeds $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. The spheres collide directly. Immediately after the collision, $A$ continues to move in its original direction with speed $0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the velocity of $B$ immediately after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the spheres caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is moving with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a smooth horizontal surface when it collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $1.5\text{ kg}$. In the collision, particle $P$ is brought to rest.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the speed of $Q$ after the collision is $2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the system caused by the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $P$ on $Q$ during the collision.

questions.prompt: Two uniform smooth spheres $A$ and $B$, of masses $3\text{ kg}$ and $1\text{ kg}$ respectively, move towards each other on a smooth horizontal surface with speeds $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. The spheres collide directly. After the collision, both spheres move in the original direction of motion of $A$, and the speed of $B$ is $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ greater than the speed of $A$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $A$ and the speed of $B$ after the collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the system caused by the collision.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is moving with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a smooth horizontal surface towards a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: In one situation, $A$ and $B$ coalesce on impact to form a single combined particle $C$. Find the speed of $C$ after the collision and determine the loss of kinetic energy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: In another situation, the particles do not coalesce. Instead, particle $A$ rebounds with speed $1.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the speed of $B$ after this collision and show that no kinetic energy is lost in this case.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$ is moving with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal track towards a stationary block $B$ of mass $1.2\text{ kg}$. On impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce to form a combined body $C$. Immediately after impact, $C$ enters a rough horizontal section of the track where the coefficient of friction between $C$ and the track is $\mu = 0.2$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $C$ immediately after the collision and calculate the kinetic energy lost during the impact.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the work-energy principle, or otherwise, find the distance $C$ travels on the rough track before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: Three particles $P$, $Q$, and $R$ have masses $m$, $m$, and $2m$ respectively and lie in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. Particle $P$ is projected with speed $u$ directly towards $Q$, which is at rest. On impact, $P$ and $Q$ coalesce to form a combined particle $S_1$ of mass $2m$. Particle $S_1$ then continues in the same line of motion and collides with $R$, which is initially at rest. On this second impact, $S_1$ and $R$ coalesce to form a single combined particle $S_2$ of mass $4m$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find, in terms of $u$, the speed of $S_1$ immediately after the first collision, and the speed of $S_2$ immediately after the second collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that $50\%$ of the initial kinetic energy of the system is lost in the first collision.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the total percentage of the initial kinetic energy of the system that is lost as a result of both collisions.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at the top of a smooth plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.32$. The distance from the release point to the bottom of the plane is $2.5\text{ m}$. At the bottom of the inclined plane, particle $A$ moves onto a smooth horizontal surface and collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$. On impact, $A$ and $B$ coalesce to form a combined particle $C$. (Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.)

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $A$ when it reaches the bottom of the plane, and show that the loss of kinetic energy caused by the collision is $\frac{4m}{m + 0.5}\text{ J}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the kinetic energy lost in the collision is $3.0\text{ J}$, find the value of $m$ and the common speed of the combined particle after the collision.
